verdict.rationale: Moss documents built-in, on-device embedding through a built-in model, and the GitHub README corroborates 'built-in embeddings', so users do not need a separate embedding pipeline for the default model. However, the only alternative to the built-in model is a 'custom' option where you bring your own precomputed vectors, which is the opposite of the database calling a configured model provider. Query-time embedding is only implied by the semantic-search docs, not stated explicitly. Missing for 10: configurable external model providers (e.g., OpenAI/Cohere) that Moss calls itself, explicit documentation of automatic query-time embedding, details on the built-in model, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can have the database generate embeddings at ingest and query time using built-in or configured model providers, instead of running a separate embedding pipeline

citations.quote: Moss embeds on-device with a built-in model, or you can bring your own vectors using a `custom` model
